conditions: Each dead contract-holder has a fixed list of named revenge targets recorded before death.
The holder must cause every named target to die; the death may occur through a direct action or a trap the holder deliberately set in motion.
The holder must know that every listed target is dead and sincerely believe the revenge is complete.
The Warden records completion; the holder returns to life at the instant their original body died.
resurrection_rule.proxy_clause: A holder may appoint a proxy only after the proxy receives the complete original contract and proof of any alteration. The proxy must understand that their action will close the holder's contract and freely choose to perform the final, contract-authorized act.
resurrection_rule.loophole: The contract governs completion of revenge, not permanent ownership of the holder's soul. An informed, voluntary proxy can perform the final authorized act. When the Warden records completion, the holder returns to life; the proxy does not automatically return.
limits: A coerced, deceived or uninformed proxy does not count.
A proxy cannot add, remove or substitute targets.
A target must be named on the original contract.
The Warden records evidence and cannot waive conditions.
Returning does not erase memories or the archive mark.

levels.name: The Awakening
levels.purpose: Teach movement through narrative discovery and establish the murder mystery.

sequence.event: Arin wakes in an abandoned transit station with no memory of the final moments.
The Warden explains that the dead world is an archive of unfinished contracts, not a place of random punishment.
Arin finds his own death record. The signature field is torn away, but a familiar route code remains.

levels.reveal: Arin was murdered, and the route code points to the gang's old dock warehouse.
levels.next_mystery: Why was Arin's death recorded as a contract-related killing?

levels.name: The Butcher
levels.purpose: Introduce the first contract-holder and expose the handler's manipulation.

sequence.event: Before Arin reaches the warehouse, Marek's own memory-echo shows that he has already killed every target on his contract, including the final dock supervisor. The Warden has not yet recorded completion because Marek refuses to accept that the final target was the person who ordered his sister's death.

Arin finds the original dispatch sheet and proves Marek's target list was altered. The evidence shows Marek's revenge is complete under the written contract, even though the handler deceived him about the targets' guilt.

Marek accepts that every name on his contract is dead and that he completed the list. The Warden records satisfaction and Marek returns to life. Arin does not kill Marek; he witnesses the contract-holder's departure from the dead world.

levels.reveal: Marek's revenge list was completed before Arin arrived. The handler manipulated Marek's understanding of guilt, but did not change the contract's fixed target list.
levels.next_mystery: Who altered the list, and why did the handler want Marek to kill Arin?

levels.name: The Strategist
levels.purpose: Reveal the proxy clause and connect Silas to Arin's murder.

sequence.event: Silas's memory-echo reveals that he set a chain of traps that killed every target on his own contract before Arin arrived. He withheld the final proof from himself because he feared that returning would expose his crimes.
Arin reconstructs the original contract and finds Silas's notes proving the final target died in the last trap. The proxy clause explains why knowledge and free choice matter.

Arin confronts Silas with the evidence. Silas accepts that every named target is dead and that his traps completed the contract. The Warden records satisfaction and Silas returns to life. The archive reveals Dev's route code and a hidden ledger location.

levels.reveal: Silas completed his target list through traps before Arin arrived. He manipulated the other contract-holders and understood the proxy clause.
levels.next_mystery: Why did Dev help arrange Arin's death, and can the contract loophole return Arin?

levels.name: The Impossible Return
levels.purpose: Execute the proxy loophole and establish the persistent connection.

sequence.event: Arin reaches the contract archive and assembles the full evidence chain.

The Warden explains that a proxy may only perform the final act still required by a contract. Arin's contract is different: its named target is the person who ordered his murder, and the evidence proves the handler's forged amendment. Arin sends Dev the full record so Dev can freely choose whether to expose the handler and complete the contract-authorized final act.

Dev, alive in the living world, receives the full evidence and freely exposes the handler by destroying the handler's control record, the final target named in Arin's original contract. The Warden verifies the evidence, records the final act and Arin returns to life.

levels.reveal: Arin returns because Dev freely performs the final act against the original named target after receiving the complete truth. This is an application of the contract's proxy clause, not a special exception.
levels.persistent_connection: The archive recorded Arin's death and return in one continuous contract entry. The mark remains as a record-link: near locations and objects tied to the contract, Arin perceives echoes and hears the Warden. It does not give him unrestricted access to the dead world.
levels.next_mystery: Why did Dev choose to help only after receiving the evidence, and what happened to him afterward?

levels.name: The Betrayer
levels.purpose: Resolve the murder, explain Dev's arrival and close the emotional arc.

sequence.event: Arin follows the dead-world echo to the location where Dev died during his attempt to destroy the ledger evidence.
Conflicting accounts are compared against the original ledger, dispatch record and Dev's recorded confession.

Dev admits he first agreed to stage Arin's death under family pressure, then chose to murder him when Arin refused to surrender the ledger, before receiving the full evidence. Later, alive in the living world and after receiving the complete contract and proof, Dev freely performed the proxy's final act by destroying the handler's control record, the original named target. The Warden verified the evidence, recorded completion, and Arin returned to life. Dev subsequently died in the evidence-room fire while trying to destroy the ledger. Arin decides whether to expose Dev's actions and preserve the evidence.

levels.reveal: Dev murdered Arin to protect his family and himself; coercion explains his first choice but does not excuse the final killing.
levels.resolution: Arin exposes the gang and preserves the ledger. He does not erase Dev's guilt or let the gang's handler escape accountability.
